subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate memoryFlush and required compaction from the foreground session/global processing lane, and if so should that be a dedicated maintenance lane or a cancellable/preemptible in-lane design?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug is real, but the repair changes scheduler fairness and session-state ordering semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Dedicated Maintenance Lane
options.body: Create a bounded compaction/memory maintenance lane with explicit transcript/session handoff rules so foreground user turns can proceed or receive a quick busy response.

options.title: Preemptible In-Lane Compaction
options.body: Keep compaction in the current lane but add a maintainer-approved cancellation/yield protocol and watchdog that can release the lane for foreground user messages.

options.title: Keep Current Mitigations
options.body: Accept the 180-second timeout and background priority as sufficient for now, leaving active compaction able to block foreground work until timeout or completion.

recommendation.title: Dedicated Maintenance Lane
recommendation.body: Create a bounded compaction/memory maintenance lane with explicit transcript/session handoff rules so foreground user turns can proceed or receive a quick busy response.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest recent history on the queued compaction wrapper and scheduler-adjacent code path.
